lines.text: One outlet in your bathroom is quietly counting electrons. And it can save your life.
A GFCI. Two buttons, no magic, just very clever arithmetic.
Current flows out on the hot wire, and comes back on the neutral. Same amount out, same amount back.
A ring around both wires compares them. Opposite currents make opposite magnetic fields, and they cancel to zero.
Now drop a hair dryer in the tub. Some current takes a shortcut, through the water, and through you.
Less comes back than went out. The ring feels a difference of just five milliamps.
That tiny signal fires a solenoid, the contacts open, and power can be gone in a fortieth of a second.
So why not just use the breaker? It waits for fifteen amps. A tenth of an amp can stop a heart, and the breaker wouldn't even notice.
Breakers protect the house. A GFCI protects you.
Press TEST every month. It makes a small fake leak. If the outlet doesn't click off, replace it.
Watch again, and see if you can spot the missing electrons.
